title: URL as State
description: Learn to treat the URL as a first-class state container in Next.js, using query parameters and route segments to drive filtering, pagination, and navigation.

data.text: The URL is one of the most underused state containers in web development. It is shareable, bookmarkable, survives page refreshes, and works with the browser's back and forward buttons. Treating the URL as state means encoding things like the active tab, search query, filters, and pagination directly in query parameters.

In Next.js, both the App Router and Pages Router give you hooks to read and write the URL. When your UI state lives in the URL, users can share filtered views with colleagues, return to a specific page after a refresh, and use browser history naturally.

Not every piece of state belongs in the URL. The URL is best for state that users should be able to bookmark, share, or navigate back to. Common candidates include: search queries, filter selections, active tabs, sort order, pagination, and modal open/closed state.

In the Next.js App Router, `useSearchParams` reads the current query string, and `useRouter` with `push` or `replace` updates it. Using `replace` instead of `push` avoids polluting browser history with every keystroke.

data.title: URL-Driven Search Filter (App Router)

data.text: In Server Components, you can read the query string directly from the request. This means URL-driven filtering works without any client-side JavaScript at all. Combine server-side `searchParams` with React Server Components for a filtering experience that is fast, SEO-friendly, and shareable.

data.title: Server Component Reading Query Params
Debounce Inputs
data.text: Never update the URL on every keystroke without debouncing. Each update creates a new history entry or replaces the current one. A 300ms debounce feels instant to users and dramatically reduces unnecessary renders and router work.

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: URL state is shareable, bookmarkable, and survives navigation
Use query parameters for filters, search, pagination, and active tabs
useSearchParams + useRouter control URL state on the client
Server Components can read query params directly without client code
